title: Under the operator's grant the agent is on the loop; the grant delegates sign-off
situation: Realizing sign-off-gates, the lead found the corpus holds no out-of-the-loop autonomy value and asked whether expressing the operator's grant as on-the-loop, scoped to delegated gates, with the delegated sign-off on the sign-off decision right, keeps the meaning.
decision: It does. In the established scale of human oversight, out of the loop means no one can intervene; under delegated authority the operator can still stop the work, so the agent is on the loop between gates and at every gate whose sign-off is delegated to it, and what the grant takes the operator out of is the loop of those sign-offs, which the sign-off decision right carries. No new autonomy value is needed.
consequences: The authority concept states this; the sign-off-gates story renders the grant this way.
